hero.caption: Erected by the Bostonian Society near the site of the Great Molasses Flood of 1919. It reads, "On January 15, 1919, a molasses tank at 529 Commercial Street exploded under pressure, killing 21 people. A 40-foot wave of molasses buckled the elevated railroad tracks, crushed buildings and inundated the neighborhood. Structural defects in the tank combined with unseasonably warm temperatures contributed to the disaster."

images.filename: Boston Molasses Flood Aftermath (original tank scale superimposed).png
images.caption: On 15 January 1919, a storage tank at the Purity Distilling Company in Boston, MA burst, releasing 2.3 million gallons of molasses. The resulting flood destroyed nearby buildings and claimed the lives of 21 people. In order to better visualize the scale of the disaster, this photograph (originally published in the Globe Newspaper shortly after the event) has been annotated to show the approximate size, shape, and location of the tank before its collapse. The scale of the overlay was estimated based on the tank's recorded dimensions and the size of human figures in this photograph (assumed to be 5-6 feet tall).
